paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The grumbling Pharisees and scribes said, "This man welcomes sinners and eats with them" (Luke 15:2), and they meant it as a complaint. Jesus answers with two parables that turn that complaint into good news. Welcoming sinners isn't a side project for Him. It's the very thing He came to do.

Now look at what the shepherd and the woman do. They don't shrug and say, "Ninety-nine is plenty, ten is close enough." The man goes after the one that is lost "until he finds it" (Luke 15:4), and the woman lights a lamp, sweeps her house, and searches carefully (Luke 15:8). And when they find what was lost, they can't keep it to themselves. They call everybody over to say, "Rejoice with me" (Luke 15:6, 9). Friend, that's how much one lost person matters to God.

So what does that mean for you? Jesus says there is "joy in the presence of God's angels over one sinner who repents" (Luke 15:10). That means when you turn back to God, heaven doesn't sigh. Heaven throws a party. I know a little about being the one nobody came looking for, and I'm telling you, being found beats being forgotten every single time. So stay close, keep your ears open like those tax collectors and sinners did, and let God's joy over you be louder than any grumbling.
